name: Classic Chakki Atta
tagline: The everyday roti flour our mill was built for.
description: 100% whole wheat, stone-ground on slow millstones so the germ, bran and flavour stay in the flour — not on the mill floor.
longDescription: This is the atta we have packed for our own family since 1978. Single-origin Sharbati-style wheat from Shekhawati is cleaned, sun-rested, then ground on traditional chakki millstones that never run hot. The result is a slightly coarse, nutty flour that drinks water well, rolls into soft phulkas, and keeps its sweetness for days. No maida blended in, no preservatives, no bleaching.

name: Organic Chakki Atta
tagline: Certified organic wheat, the same slow stone.
description: India Organic certified wheat from partner farms, ground on the same millstones as our classic atta — just a cleaner field behind it.
longDescription: A handful of families in Sikar and Jhunjhunu have grown wheat for us without synthetic pesticides for more than a decade. We mill their grain in small lots, never mixed with conventional wheat, and pack it the same week. Soft rotis, a faintly sweet aroma, and the quiet confidence of a certified organic supply chain.

name: Multigrain Chakki Atta
tagline: Five grains, one dough, softer everyday rotis.
description: Whole wheat with jowar, bajra, ragi and barley — each grain stone-ground separately, then blended in our mill kitchen.
longDescription: Multigrain only works when every grain is milled with care. We grind wheat, jowar, bajra, ragi and barley on the chakki, then blend them so the dough still rolls without cracking. Higher fibre, a gentle nuttiness, and rotis that stay soft in the tiffin.

name: Chakki Besan
tagline: Slow-ground chana dal with the fragrance intact.
description: Gram flour stone-ground from split chickpeas — silky enough for kadhi, robust enough for pakoras.
longDescription: Most commercial besan is roller-milled and left sitting in warehouses. Ours is ground from unpolished chana dal on cool millstones, so the natural oils stay in the flour. You will smell the difference when it hits hot oil.

name: Jowar Atta
tagline: Gluten-free sorghum, ground for bhakri and modern kitchens.
description: Naturally gluten-free jowar, stone-ground to a fine, pale flour that binds with a little warm water.
longDescription: Jowar is one of the oldest grains of the Deccan — and one of the gentlest on the stomach. We mill whole sorghum slowly so the flour stays pale, slightly sweet, and easy to roll into bhakri or blend into wheat dough.

name: Bajra Atta
tagline: Winter millet from Rajasthan, ground the village way.
description: Pearl millet stone-ground into a warm, grey-gold flour — the taste of winter raab and thick rotis.
longDescription: Bajra is the grain of our home state. We source it from rain-fed farms, mill it fresh (it does not like to sit), and recommend finishing a pack within six weeks. Earthy, filling, and rich in iron.

name: Ragi Atta
tagline: Finger millet for porridge, dosa, and stronger bones.
description: Whole ragi, stone-ground to a fine chocolate-brown flour — naturally rich in calcium.
longDescription: Ragi is the quiet powerhouse of South Indian kitchens. We mill the whole seed, bran and all, so the flour is dark, malty, and perfect for kanji, dosa, cookies, or a spoonful blended into wheat atta.

name: Chakki Dalia
tagline: Broken wheat, cracked on the same stones as our atta.
description: Coarse, toasted-sweet dalia for porridge, khichdi and salads — not the dusty broken wheat of a roller mill.
longDescription: After the millstones have done their work, we keep a coarser cut of the same wheat as dalia. It cooks into a nutty porridge, a light khichdi, or a lemon-and-cucumber salad that actually tastes of grain.
